About Me

I am a second-year MPH student in Epidemiology with a certificate in Applied Biostatistics and Public Health Data Science at Columbia University. I started this journey at McGill University, where I majored in Environment with a concentration in Ecological Determinants of Health in Society and minors in Statistics and Field Studies.

While at Columbia, I have really fallen in love with biostatistics. Partaking in research outside of my immediate interests has demonstrated that what I love is the story the numbers tell, no matter the subject matter. I want others to have this love as well, which has led me to become a Teaching Assistant for the Quantitative Methods of Public Health course at Mailman. I loved how the courses I took for my statistics minor in undergrad challenged me, and have carried this knowledge into my applied biostatistics courses.

Recently, I have also embraced my interest in gastroenterological research by getting involved with GI research at Columbia, including co-authoring a paper on treatment patterns in eosinophilic esophagitis. I hope to continue pursuing this interest in my future career. I have also done research on antimicrobial resistance, often called the “silent pandemic,” which I am now extending into my master’s thesis.

Presenting our AMR survey at the AUA Annual Meeting in Las Vegas (2025)

Outside of research, I’ve volunteered with Pothawira, a clinic, school, and orphanage in Malawi, since 2018. In 2023 I climbed Mount Kilimanjaro to raise money for the clinic’s surgical center. I also cheered competitively for 12 years and coached McGill’s Level 4 team, fueling my excitement about teaching. At Columbia, I am on the executive board for CIPHER, a club involved with volunteering in the Washington Heights community and spreading public health literacy. I also run the Mailman Jewish Student Association as co-president.

Uhuru Peak, raising funds for Pothawira’s surgical center (2023)

One last stunt before graduation (2025)

Travelling has always been a big passion of mine. During my time at McGill, I completed two field study semesters: one in Kenya and Tanzania in 2023 and one in Panama in 2024. Though neither of these programs was necessarily health-related, they emphasized how much health depends on one’s surroundings, and I was thrilled at the opportunity to weave field work into my undergraduate studies.

I am originally from the South Shore of Massachusetts, just outside Boston. I have my advanced PADI scuba diving certification, and becoming a Divemaster is one of my dreams! I have a rescue dog named Enzo who I will make sure to weave into any conversation. For anyone curious, he was found as a stray and brought into the NYCACC public shelter, and he is estimated to be about 8 years old and is a Yorkie-Pekingese mix (courtesy of the Embark DNA tests).
